overview: Each search server builds an in-memory quadtree (leaf ≤ 100 businesses) at startup from the DB; rebuilt nightly with rolling restarts.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative directory: 100M businesses, 100 B of geo-index payload each.
estimation.calculation: 100,000,000 × 100 B ≈ 10 GB of index payload before tree/replica overhead.
estimation.result: Replicating the complete tree on every server is expensive.
estimation.implication: Shard by geographic region and replicate hot regions; use exact-distance filtering for cell-boundary correctness.

entityDetails.purpose: Authoritative business location and searchable attributes.
accessPatterns: Create/update a business; hydrate candidate IDs from a geo index.
constraints: Validate coordinates; exact-distance filtering removes false positives from cell traversal.

apiDetails.rationale: Search every intersecting cell, then exact-distance filter and rank. A fixed nine-cell scan is only sufficient for a bounded radius/cell-size combination. Bind cursors to the query center/radius and stable distance/ID ordering.

apiDetails.purpose: Register a business and update the derived geo index.
apiDetails.rationale: Publish index changes through a durable change feed; document freshness if rebuilding periodically.

steps.title: App → LB → Search Service → In-memory quadtrees
steps.explanation: Traverse quadtree leaves intersecting the search circle; dense regions split more deeply.

steps.title: Search Service → Businesses
steps.explanation: Hydrate candidates and apply exact-distance, active-state and category filtering.

steps.title: Nightly index rebuild → In-memory quadtrees
steps.explanation: Build the new tree off the serving path; atomically swap the version across healthy replicas.

failureCases.scenario: Geo index is stale after a business moves
failureCases.handling: Version the source record and index update; rebuild or replay changes. Filter inactive/deleted businesses during hydration and expose a defined freshness bound.

alternatives: Use geohash cells for simple incremental indexing, searching all cells intersecting the radius. Use region-sharded quadtrees for density-adaptive searches when building and atomically swapping in-memory trees is acceptable.
